description: Every Make (formerly Integromat) Management API operation from the terminal, plus blocking agent runs, git-backed blueprint sync, dev-to-prod promote with ID remap, and a cross-team DLQ inbox no other tool has.

novel_features.name: Blocking scenario run for agents
novel_features.description: Trigger a scenario and block until it finishes, returning the execution result as one JSON envelope. Composes /scenarios/{id}/run + executions polling + bundle fetch.
novel_features.rationale: Make's API returns immediately with an executionId; agents need the actual result. make-cli has no --wait; cloud MCP is paid-tier and Anthropic-hosted only.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs a Make scenario's output to decide its next step, this is the only command that returns the bundle inline.

novel_features.name: Git-backed blueprint sync
novel_features.description: Export every scenario's blueprint into a local repo as canonical JSON, one file per scenario, with a separate sidecar for metadata noise. Commit-ready.
novel_features.rationale: Make's UI has no first-party git story; community runs DIY scenarios to push blueprints to GitHub daily because nothing else does. Canonicalization makes diffs meaningful.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets an agent or human treat scenarios as code: review diffs, restore prior versions, run CI on changes.

novel_features.name: Dev to prod scenario promote with auto-remap
novel_features.description: Promote a scenario from one team to another, rewriting connectionId/hookId/dataStoreId/folderId via auto-suggested name match or a user-edited YAML map. Dry-run shows the rewrites.
novel_features.rationale: Make's #1 community request: blueprint import is lossy because IDs don't remap. Cloud MCP and make-cli ignore this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when a Make scenario needs to ship from dev to prod — the only command that solves the ID-remap problem.

novel_features.name: Cross-scenario DLQ inbox
novel_features.description: List incomplete executions across all scenarios in one or many teams, group by error-reason fingerprint, bulk retry or resolve with a regex match.
novel_features.rationale: Make's UI is per-scenario only; nothing surfaces patterns across an account. Requires the local mirror to join across scenarios.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When triaging Make failures, this is the only command that shows everything that broke and groups by why.

novel_features.name: Connections audit
novel_features.description: Find connections that are unused, expiring, or repeatedly errored. Joins local connections with walked blueprint references and execution errors.
novel_features.rationale: Make's Connections UI shows a flat list with no usage, expiry, or error data. No API endpoint exposes whether a connection is used by any active scenario.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run before a prod cutover, or weekly to catch stale OAuth tokens before they 401 your scenarios.

novel_features.name: Cross-team scenario list
novel_features.description: Union scenarios across every team the token can see, with last-edit, last-run, error rate, folder path, active flag. Filter by --stale Nh.
novel_features.rationale: Make's API forces one teamId per call; the UI is single-team-at-a-time. The local mirror lets us union.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Monday-morning ritual command: what is active and what is stale across everything you own.

novel_features.name: Webhook to scenario routing map
novel_features.description: For each webhook, show which scenarios consume it by walking every blueprint's gateway:CustomWebHook references. Flag orphan hooks (no consumer) and shared hooks (multiple consumers).
novel_features.rationale: Make's UI shows hooks and scenarios on separate screens; there is no hook-to-scenario reverse map anywhere.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When a webhook misroutes or you are cleaning up old hooks, this tells you what is actually connected.

novel_features.name: Blueprint diff and restore
novel_features.description: Diff two blueprint snapshots from the local snapshot table; restore re-PUTs a snapshot via the API. Structural diff ignores the metadata.expect/restore noise.
novel_features.rationale: Make's UI version history is shallow and ephemeral; there is no diff or rollback tool. Our snapshot table outlives Make's history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: After a blueprint promote went wrong, this is the rollback path — git log + git restore for Make scenarios.
